summary: The failures cluster around negative and boundary time-point decomposition: whole seconds and subseconds appear to be split with truncation toward zero, producing inconsistent calendar fields and negative fractions. The current source excerpts do not show the complete system-time formatter or duration conversion contract needed to confirm the repair site and boundary behavior.
hypotheses: System-time formatting splits epoch duration into seconds and remainder using truncation toward zero, so negative fractional timestamps produce incorrect calendar and subsecond fields.
Subsecond conversion or signed-to-unsigned formatting mishandles negative remainders, especially at the minimum nanosecond value.
Duration-ratio normalization in the system-time formatter loses carry or borrow when converting nonstandard clock periods.
